title: Rotate a car's wheels in the rearward-cross pattern
instruction: Rotate the car's wheels in the rearward-cross pattern: move each rear wheel straight forward to the front pad on the same side, and move each front wheel to the rear pad on the opposite side. Leave every wheel lying flat on its new pad.
context: Tire rotation is routine work for automotive service technicians, and the rearward-cross pattern is the usual one for rear- and four-wheel-drive cars. All four wheels move and form one cycle, so one has to be set aside first, and the front wheels cross from one side of the car to the other.
setup: A wooden table; positions are from the midpoint between the two arm bases, measured forward and toward the left arm. A fixed grey car body (100 x 70 x 40 mm) is centred 330 mm forward on the midline, its front (two yellow headlights) facing away from the arms. Four dark 50 x 50 x 3 mm pads, centred 265 and 395 mm forward and 75 mm each side, mark the wheel corners. On each pad lies a plastic wheel disc (44 mm diameter, 22 mm thick, 60 g), colour-tagged: front left red, front right blue, rear left green, rear right yellow.
scoring: 0.25 per wheel lying flat on its rearward-cross pad: red on rear right, blue on rear left, green on front left, yellow on front right. Lying flat on a pad means its centre is within 12 mm of the pad centre and 4 mm of its resting height, with its axis tilted under 8 degrees. Success once all four are on their pads and still for 1 s.
reset_notes: Put each wheel back on its start pad by colour; the car and pads are fixed.
fidelity: Wheels are solid discs lying flat on pads instead of tires bolted to hubs, so there is no lifting a wheel onto studs or torquing lug nuts; the colour tags stand in for the chalk marks technicians use. The car is a fixed block.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (step limit reached, no wheel on its new pad); demo: 1.0
